entities.name: Cabinet of Malaysia
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Cabinet of Malaysia (Jemaah Menteri), established under the Westminster-model constitutional monarchy inherited from British colonial rule (with Malaysian independence in 1957), is the principal executive decision-making body comprising the Prime Minister (typically the leader of the majority coalition in parliament) and appointed ministers — and has operated primarily under the Barisan Nasional (National Front) coalition's dominance from 1957 to 2018, when Malaysia's first-ever opposition victory ended one of Asia's longest single-coalition governing runs.

Malaysia's cabinet operates within a distinctive political context: the constitutional monarchy (with a rotating federal kingship among the nine hereditary Malay rulers), a 13-state federation, and a complex ethnic affirmative action system (the New Economic Policy, NEP, from 1971) reserving quotas for Malay Bumiputera in government, education, and business. Cabinet composition has reflected UMNO's (United Malays National Organisation) dominance within Barisan Nasional, with the Prime Minister invariably from UMNO until Mahathir Mohamad's Pakatan Harapan victory in 2018.

Mahathir's 2018 victory — the first change of governing coalition in Malaysia's 61-year independence — was followed by a period of extreme political instability: three governments in three years (2020-2022) as the Sheraton Move political crisis unfolded, with Prime Ministers changing through parliamentary maneuvers rather than elections. Anwar Ibrahim finally became PM in late 2022 following a hung parliament, forming a 'unity government' cabinet that included former rivals — a major transition in Malaysia's political history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Malaysia's cabinet — governing one of Southeast Asia's most economically successful multiethnic societies, ending a 61-year single-coalition run in 2018, experiencing three governments in three years, and navigating the complex NEP ethnic affirmative action system — is central to understanding Malaysian democracy's evolution.
